line: You play? Don't just stand there breathing on the board. Sit down or move along.
A little. That's what Lin said, and he took my rook in nine moves. I'm Walt. White or black?
Pawn to e4. Lin's late. Wednesdays he drives his wife to the market on Eighth. Your move. Don't take all day.
Book move. Fine. You live around here, or just cutting through the park?
choice1: I live on Grand, near the library.

line: Huh. Lin does that. Thinks it rattles me. It doesn't. Who taught you?
choice1: My dad, mostly. We lived on Grand.
choice2: I should go. Good game so far.

line: Grand. My wife's dentist was up there, over the bakery. Both gone now, the bakery and the dentist. Check, by the way.
choice3: I should head out. Thanks for the game.

line: Bishop. Sure. Here comes Lin, walking like he owns the park. You want to keep the seat, or watch him beat me properly?
choice2: Let him have it. I should go.

line: Smart. Lin, this is {playerName}, from Grand. Don't go easy, they'll get soft.
Back for more? Lin's late. You can keep his seat warm till he shows.
Thirty-one years at the plant, and the best thing I got out of it was a guy on the line who taught me the Sicilian. Funny what sticks.
Barbershop had that president on again. Whole room nodding along. I just wanted a haircut.
choice1: You didn't want to get into it?
choice2: He's got a point about some things.

line: My daughter's all lit up about the new president. I told her I'll get excited when the 14 bus runs on time.
choice2: You could let her have it.

line: Lin says you've been at that center on Grand a lot. Says the tea's better there. I told him tea is tea.
You're out here more than the pigeons. Lin wants a rematch, by the way. Says you got lucky.
Board's taken.
choice1: Fair. I was rude last time.

line: Not now. Thinking.
If you're after the sports section, you'll wait. I paid for this paper in taxes, I'm reading all of it.
choice1: I'll take the front page, then.

line: Front page is the same every day anyway. I'm Walt. They stopped delivering to my block in March. Twenty-six years I had the Ledger on my step.
They called forty-one twenty minutes ago. I'm forty-six. Don't take that chair, the spring's gone.
Walt. Blood pressure, every three months, so my daughter stops calling. It's always fine. They take it twice anyway, like they don't believe the first one.
choice1: Mine goes up just sitting here.

line: Walt lowers the paper an inch. "They moved the crossword to page nine. Nobody asked me."
choice1: Want a second pair of eyes on it?

line: You sick, or just keeping me company? They've got the cooking channel on again. Nobody in this room is allowed to eat any of it.
Walt sees you, and goes back to his paper.
choice1: Sorry I was rude last time, Walt.

line: You're in here as much as me lately. Dana asked if you were my grandkid. I told her my grandkids don't read the obituaries.
choice1: Anybody we know in them today?
